I-1.answer: New source per call without ids
I-1.reading: A bare write() with no caller or source id is its own new source; idempotency applies only when an id is passed (documented for retrying callers).

I-2.reading: Never invent 'now', but extract every temporal signal: anchor order explicit date in text > the line's own date > nearest dated line of the same source > session order > recorded_at. Every extracted time carries `basis` and `precision` (exact/day/month/year/relative/unknown); weak anchors are kept and labelled, never presented as exact. Temporal relations are extracted even without absolute dates (before/after, durations, 'since', 'for N years', counts per period) for the temporal leg.

I-3.reading: One output token: the cited lines say the earlier value no longer holds; the conflict ladder reads it as the transition hint (Q7).

I-4.answer: Quarantined derived items stored inert with reasons
I-4.reading: Same as gate 1 for raw: never retrieved, visible to audit and N1 forensics, releasable by review.

I-5.reading: Facts about a pending_merge entity are keyed on a provisional id and searchable at once; a later merge re-points them through key aliases (M-17).

I-6.answer: Contest when only one side is dated
I-6.reading: Event time when both are dated, recorded time when neither; one dated side -> keep both as contested; the ladder records the basis.

I-7.reading: With a worker model configured, L3 is on by default: edges compiled from every fact, written to the graph store (Ladybug / SQL adjacency embedded, Neo4j server), and the graph read leg runs when the router asks for it (its own screen before it counts in results). Amends Q1: default layers are L0, L1 and L3; L2, L4, L5 stay opt-in.

I-8.reading: Recall blocks carry a marker; the fingerprints of blocks rendered by the session's last read are kept; an assistant turn overlapping them is an echo: kept as L0 raw, no facts derived from the echoed part, never counted as support. User restatement counts as assent, not echo.

I-9.answer: CONTEXT: up to 3 lines, max 200 tokens
I-9.reading: Up to 3 previous live, unquarantined lines of the same source, never cited.

OF-1.reading: sleep() enqueues a job and returns a handle {job_id, status} at once; `await handle.wait()` or `await memory.wait_for_pending()` waits (eval harness and tests only). Per namespace at most one running job and one pending follow-up: concurrent sleep() calls coalesce onto the same follow-up handle. Jobs hold a persisted lease and resume from per-stage watermarks after a crash.

OF-2.answer: Triggers: (N deposits AND M idle) OR C context pressure (owner)
OF-2.reading: Full sleep when N new deposits AND M minutes idle; compression when context (working) memory passes C, configurable, default 70% of the context budget. A minimum gap K applies to BOTH trigger kinds (owner). Values are configuration, calibrated on measured cost per cycle.

OF-3.answer: Fold v1 stages into the decided order
OF-3.reading: Miners become flag-selected modes of catch-up extraction, rule_edges joins reconcile, the sleep_compute hook is replaced by the stage registry; each mode is retired unless a screen keeps it.

OF-4.reading: Per namespace, on time alone (default daily): retention, due watches, decay, compression, log prune; no model calls.

OF-5/6.answer: Job pool per profile, oldest dirty first
OF-5/6.reading: 1 concurrent namespace job on embedded SQLite, configurable (default 4) on the server profile; oldest dirty namespace first; one global semaphore matched to model-server slots.

RT-1.reading: Every job is written to the SQL outbox in the same transaction as its event; taskiq carries job ids to workers (InMemoryBroker in library mode; Redis/NATS/RabbitMQ broker and separate worker processes in server mode); a worker marks the row done; unfinished rows are re-sent on start.

RT-2.reading: All orchestration async (TaskGroup, timeouts, cancellation); GPU encoders (embedder, Jina) each in one dedicated thread executor with micro-batching; blocking DB/index I/O in a bounded thread pool; model calls async over HTTP behind a global semaphore; a process pool only for CPU-heavy parsing.

RT-3.reading: 1 interactive read, 2 write hot path, 3 online extraction (calls 1 and 2), 4 sleep and maintenance; higher classes go first, lower classes keep a guaranteed minimum share.

RT-4.reading: Windows coalesce into larger batches, the oldest backlog is marked underived (raw stays searchable), writes never block; backlog-age metric and alert.

MOD-1.reading: StageRegistry, LegRegistry, BackendRegistry, ProviderRegistry, PromptRegistry with Protocols; built-ins register at import, third parties via Python entry points; config names parts; the LayerRegistry decides what runs.

MOD-2.reading: Async-native providers with scopes app / job / request (engine lifetime, one background job, one read); finalisers close DB and model clients; tests override providers with fakes; the clock is a provider.

MOD-3.reading: Layered contract: api -> (ingest, derive, read, compose) -> (store, models, trust, runtime) -> schemas/core types; store never imports read or derive; read never imports derive.

MOD-4.reading: memspine.schemas holds every step's typed input and output with a schema version; JSON Schema exported to docs/v2/schemas/ so docs and code never drift; upcasters for old versions.

R-Q1.reading: pool -> lift -> one Jina call, so every shown turn has its own score.

R-Q2.reading: The 1-call target is amended for the deep tier only.

R-Q3.reading: 300 ms p95 without rerank (CPU), 350 ms p95 with Jina on GPU; both in CI on a reference box.

R-Q4.reading: Every tier, deep calibrated at 64; no silent zero scores.

R-Q5.answer: Multi-party flag; no viewer = shared only
R-Q5.reading: Write path sets the flag on a second participant or visibility tag; viewerless reads see owner-shared and unmarked records only (fixes today's no-filter read).

R-Q6.answer: Gate fires: keep stable prefix, drop evidence
R-Q6.reading: Persona, profile card and standing answers stay; prompt caching keeps working.

R-Q7/8.answer: Retire full/compose modes and v1 headers
R-Q7/8.reading: Facts fold into the single-pool notes block; profile card stays as [profile]; anything a screen proves useful comes back.
